collection.credit:
* V9 "Age of Terrible Ideas": event prose, material applications,
  trial and consequence branches by ChatGPT. Core requests for intense
  conflict, fights, false guilt, courts, imprisonment, reconciliation,
  and the sixteen specific bizarre materials by Lorsieab2.

ledger.why: the Building effects on the ending pages; the optional modest Tech is one of two equal copies of each ending

items.text: The rivals refuse to speak for a week, then exchange tools without a word.
Both leave the hearing convinced they won. The leader is exhausted.
The wall stands crooked. Nobody wants to touch it again.
A child paints a sign reading 'PLEASE DO NOT ARGUE NEAR THE WALL.'
The rivalry continues, but neither is allowed to make unproven accusations.
'I still think your wall is ugly.' / 'I still think you're impossible.' They shake hands anyway.
(Subject) admits the public accusation hurt more than the failed project. (Friend) listens, then says, 'Yes. It did.'
The two build a better wall together and refuse to call it friendship.
A child asks whether they are friends now. Both shout, 'NO!' in unison.
(Friend) leaves a small bag of clean shell powder at (Subject)'s door. The note reads, 'Try not to ruin it this time.'

intro.name: The coating
intro.text:
Two builders, (Subject) and (Friend), have disliked each other ever since (Subject) called (Friend)'s favorite bench 'an architectural apology.'
Now (Subject) unveils a revolutionary wall coating made from {v9_materials}. (Friend) declares it {a masterpiece|a fraud|a waste of good materials|a personal attack on the discipline of Building}.
At sunrise, the wall has {cracked|turned purple|started shedding flakes|acquired a horrifying smell|become unexpectedly beautiful}.

text_only.reason: a story rivalry between two villagers, not a preference

question.name: Sabotage!
question.text: (Subject) accuses (Friend) of sabotage. (Friend) is so furious that (friend.he/she) kicks an EMPTY basket across the workshop.

choices.label: Let the builders confront one another before the leader.
Ask the apprentices and children what they saw.
Separate the rivals and repair the wall first.

i1.text: Tool marks suggest deliberate interference, but the marks match the inventor's own tools.

i2.text: The missing ingredient is discovered in (Friend)'s workshop; a receipt proves (friend.he/she) bought an identical batch.

i3.text: The wall failed because the mixture was poorly prepared.

i4.text: A third builder secretly altered it to win a commission.

i5.text: Nothing is conclusive. The accusation must not become a conviction.

hearing.text: The village leader convenes a public hearing. The rivals interrupt one another so often that the leader threatens to charge them both with wasting everyone's afternoon.

h1.text: (Subject) bursts into tears from humiliation, then grows furious at being seen crying.

h2.text: (Friend) admits to insulting the invention, but denies touching it.

h3.text: Both admit they have been spreading cruel rumors.

h4.text: (Friend) shouts, 'I HATE YOUR GUTS!' and (Subject) replies, 'THE FEELING IS MUTUAL!' The leader orders a recess.

w1.text: A child saw a figure near the wall, but cannot identify the person.

w2.text: An apprentice saw (Subject) add the wrong powder.

w3.text: An elder remembers (Friend) lending (Subject) a tool. The rivals had forgotten that brief moment of cooperation.

w4.text: A child confesses to 'ruining the wall' because (child.he/she) dropped a pebble nearby. The leader explains that guilt requires evidence.

p1.text: The wall is salvaged. The rivals argue about whose repair worked.

p2.text: The wall collapses harmlessly into an empty work area. Nobody is hurt. Both builders stare in absolute silence.

text_only.reason: the coated wall is a workshop piece, not one of the game's structures

p3.text: (Friend) quietly helps without asking for credit.

p4.text: (Subject) refuses assistance, then apologizes after exhausting (subject.himself/herself).

evidence.text: The leader announces that an accusation is not proof.

e1.text: (Subject) withdraws the allegation and apologizes awkwardly.

e2.text: (Friend) demands a public apology and receives one.

e3.text: (Subject) cannot yet apologize. The hearing ends without a verdict.

fault.text: The notes show that (Subject) accidentally substituted {v9_materials} for the intended ingredient. (Subject) {laughs helplessly|looks ill|tries to blame the handwriting|admits the mistake}.

f1.text: The rival offers a correction, without gloating.

f2.text: The rival gloats spectacularly. The leader orders (friend.him/her) to stop.

f3.text: The inventor admits guilt for the failure but not for the rumor.

sabotage.text: A third adult admits to damaging the wall out of envy.

s1.text: The culprit pays for repairs through supervised work and apologizes.

s2.text: The culprit refuses to apologize; the leader imposes proportionate restitution, and the rivals remain angry.

s3.text: The culprit claims (Friend) put (culprit.him/her) up to it. The allegation is investigated separately, not treated as established fact.
